title: NT 201 Intravesical Administration Using Vibe System (ViXe Combination Product) for the Treatment of Idiopathic Overactive Bladder
official: RELIEVE (RandomizEd triaL of Intravesical xEomin for incontinence via the VibE system) - a randomized, prospective, multicenter, double blind, placebo and sham controlled study to assess the safety and efficacy of NT 201 intravesical administration using Vibe System in the treatment of female participants suffering from idiopathic overactive bladder
summary: Main objective: To determine the safety and efficacy of the ViXe Combination Product for the treatment of UI in participants with OAB

interventions.name: CLOSTRIDIUM BOTULINUM NEUROTOXIN TYPE A (150KD), FREE OF COMPLEXING PROTEINS

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Signed written informed consent
2. Participants on tricyclic antidepressants, Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRI) and Serotonin-Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (SNRI) drugs should be on stable dose for at least 3 months prior to enrollment and agree to remain on stable medication consumption until the 12-week follow-up visit
3. Participant of childbearing potential must have a negative pregnancy test at screening and will practice an acceptable method of birth control, during the study and 3 months after study completion NOTE: acceptable methods of birth control are those that result in a failure rate of less than 1% per year
4. Female aged 18-80
5. Participant with known idiopathic Overactive Bladder (OAB) condition based on medical records for at least 6 months prior to enrollment
6. Participant with at least 8 daily urinary output episodes on average during a 3-day voiding diary
7. Participant with at least 5 UI episodes during a 3-day voiding diary and at least 1 per day
8. Participant who can understand and comply with the requirements of the study
9. Participant is willing and able to initiate self-catheterization, post treatment, if required
10. Participant agrees to attend all follow-up evaluations and is willing and capable of filling out voiding diaries and questionnaires and is willing to complete required exams and tests
11. Participants on antimuscarinics and/or beta-3 adrenergic agonists drugs should be on a stable dose for at least 1 month prior to screening and agree to remain on stable medication consumption until the 12-week follow-up visit
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participant with suspected retention or with Post Void Residue (PVR)> 150 ml, as measured during screening. Post void residual may be repeated one week after first assessment if the original value is greater than 150 ml
2. Participant is pregnant or breastfeeding
3. Participant with history of evidence of pelvic, urological or urogenital abnormality that in the determination of the investigator would interfere with study conduct
4. Participant with known or suspected overactive bladder caused by any neurological conditions (neuromuscular disorders such as Myasthenia Gravis, ALS, Eaton-Lambert Syndrome, Alzheimer's, Parkinson, MS, stroke (CVA), etc.)
5. Participant with a documented history or current neuromuscular disorders (e.g., myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or other conditions associated with impaired neuromuscular transmission)
6. Participant with known polyuria/polydipsia based on medical history
7. Participant with a documented prior diagnosis of reduced bladder capacity of 100ml or lower
8. Participant with variation in diuretics consumption within the last 3 months
9. Participant with known bladder outlet obstruction (BOO)
10. Participant with current or planned treatment with drugs that interfere with neuromuscular transmission (e.g., aminoglycoside, polypeptide antibiotics, lincomycin antibiotics, or aminoquinolines as well as tubocurarine-type muscle relaxants)
11. Participant with current or known recurrent urinary tract infection (3 or more infections in the last 6 months), or presence of urinary fistula, or urinary tract obstruction such as cancer, urethral stricture or presence of urinary stone
12. Participant who has received botulinum toxin injections for any condition within the past 9 months
13. Participant who has received neurostimulation for the treatment of OAB in the last 6 months
14. Participant on any active biofeedback, pelvic muscle rehabilitation, or pelvic floor physical therapy within the past 4 weeks (Self-performed Kegels exercises are allowed)
15. Participant who was nonresponsive to prior botulinum toxin treatment for OAB
16. Participant with known hypersensitivity to any botulinum toxin serotype
17. Participant with known hypersensitivity to polyurethane
18. 20.	Participant with more than minimal level of suspected stress incontinence or mixed incontinence with stress component likely to confound study outcome, based on a 3-day voiding diary or medical history, or when stress incontinence score in the MESA incontinence questionnaire is higher than the urgency incontinence score.
